title: Control room completeness: Resources live, Product Contract dossier on the goal, every daemon read has a screen
description:
Filed by architect-16a01670 from parent task-e7a3d643bde34da7b27495dbda745739 (epic breakdown, human-directed 2026-09-04).

UI GAP (human DoD 'we should have our product also ui'; memory ui-connect-everything-built-2026-09-02; re-measured 2026-09-04 at main 68eb1c5d after PR #23 the board): the Resources nav is FROZEN with a SOON chip (`apps/control-room/src/v2/shell/shell-model.ts:111`, nav-rail.tsx:120, context-bar.tsx:11-20); `/product-contract/gate-1/read` and `/documents/dossier/read` have no screen; planning.write, graph.supersede, cutover.*, work.* are unconnected by design (keep them forensic). The opened goal now opens on the six-column board (PR #23: v2/board/board-screen.tsx, board-columns.ts, board-feed.tsx).

FEATURE: (a) Resources screen live - the project's measured resources from existing reads: repository (root, branch, HEAD), provider (CLI, credential source - never a value), store (path, size, last backup), policy revision, seat limit; one fact per row, refusals verbatim, no SOON chip. (b) Product Contract dossier on the opened goal: the approved revision's personas/journeys, requirements, criteria (with coverage state), assumptions and unresolved decisions, versions - consumed from `/product-contract/gate-1/read` through the 8-touchpoint pattern. (c) Document dossier on the PRD panel from `/documents/dossier/read`. (d) An 'Advanced' forensic view behind a toggle listing the remaining raw reads (events, work items) so nothing served is unreachable. (e) A design pass with the apple-design-skill and frontend-design skills (owner's ask 2026-09-02: 'we need it for humans not bots') recorded in a row comment with the fixes applied; sources stay ASCII-only (glyphs.ts) and JSX text stays apostrophe-free (scheduler package-boundary scan, memory board-screen-landed-2026-09-04).

RULE: bidirectional roster - every daemon read route (enumerated from the listener dispatch, not a constant) is consumed by at least one screen, and every screen's read exists.
definitionOfDone: Resources screen renders measured rows against a REAL daemon; the resources nav entry carries no SOON chip (test on shell-model/nav-rail updated, `grep -c SOON` on the resources entry = 0); nav roster tests updated.

The opened goal shows the Product Contract dossier from `/product-contract/gate-1/read` (approved revision id, requirements count, criteria with coverage state); exact-key decoder and every digest mirror updated (packages generated-coverage.test.ts, apps/control-room/src/data/data-adapter.test.ts, v2/goals/approve-plan.test.tsx).

Bidirectional roster test: the served read routes (enumerated from apps/daemon/src/http/http-listener-read-dispatch.ts) equal the routes the control-room client consumes, asserted as set-equality (not subset).
Design review pass recorded in a row comment: skills used, findings, fixes applied, before/after screenshots from the live lane.

Playwright journeys for Resources and the contract dossier against a REAL daemon; gates quoted with count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`, `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test:e2e:browser`.
taskRails: FULL VERTICAL SLICE (human DoD 2026-09-04): this row ships daemon + control-room UI + tests + docs for its feature and carries NO dependsOn on any sibling row of this epic. If the plan exceeds the daemon's thresholds (12 steps / 10 files), the planning architect SPIDR-splits into children under THIS row (parentTaskId); children may depend on each other, never on a sibling feature row.

FEATURES ONLY (human DoD 2026-09-04): no security-boundary or policy work in this row. The verifier stays the documented trusted-workspace v0.1 limitation; signing, hermetic verification and freeze manifests are out of scope.

HUMAN GATES ARE HUMAN-ONLY: every approve/decide kind this row adds is operator-only, listed in HUMAN_ONLY_STEPS and MCP-excluded; every refusal carries a stable code asserted by a test (global rail 1); roster tests are bidirectional set-equality (global rail 9). A new daemon read/command follows the 8-touchpoint + .js bridge pattern (memory ui-connect-everything-built-2026-09-02).

PROVE IT LIVE: besides an offline e2e over a REAL daemon (no fixtures), completion records a live drive on the lane (UnAI at D:/projexts/UnAI or a fresh project): transcript, store path and sha in a row comment (keep each comment under 4500 chars). Never restart the wrapper to unstick a seat (claim TTL 30 min, memory real-seat-cannot-release-its-claim-2026-09-04).

implementationPlan.description: SPIDR ROLL-UP GATE. This row is a parent shell: all work lives in its three children and it carries dependsOn on every one. Confirm each is DONE — task-2ee775b319cb496fad9256c84d24744c (Resources live, no SOON chip), task-1c9587ed1b2b4e1abd6b51396ee672f8 (the Product Contract and PRD dossiers), task-bc4617d6f84f4213a00c9b1786622577 (the bidirectional route roster, the forensic view, the design pass and the live drive) — recording each landing sha and its completionSummary/reviewSummary. Per global rail 11 read those rather than re-measuring HEAD. If any is short, report_blocked with blockedOnTaskIds naming it. Write no production code in this step.

RECONCILE THE DoD, AND CORRECT ONE STALE PREMISE, in a step note. DoD 1 (Resources live, no SOON chip, nav roster updated) -> child task-2ee775b3. DoD 2 (the contract dossier and its decoder/digest mirrors) -> child task-1c9587ed. DoD 3 (the bidirectional route roster), DoD 4 (the design pass comment) and DoD 5 (Playwright + gates) -> child task-bc4617d6. THE STALE PREMISE, measured by the architect at plan time and carried into child 1's description: this row says Resources is 'FROZEN with a SOON chip (apps/control-room/src/v2/shell/shell-model.ts:111)'. `grep -n SOON apps/control-room/src/v2/shell/shell-model.ts` returns NOTHING — :110-111 is the nav entry's label and icon. The real mechanism is the per-entry `live: boolean` flag declared at shell-model.ts:25, with nav-rail.tsx:112-124 rendering the SOON StatusChip (testid `cr.nav.<id>.unavailable`) when an entry is unavailable. Record that so QA grades the rendered marker rather than a grep for a string that was never in that file.

RUN THE FULL GATE SET AT THE INTEGRATED TREE. Each leg standalone and foreground with its `Test Files N passed` count line quoted VERBATIM; an exit-0 leg with no count line is a vacuous run (global rail 8). Legs: `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`, `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test:e2e:browser`, and `pnpm test` — the root lane IS real evidence here because child 2 touched the packages digest mirrors, though it still covers NO apps/** (global rail 18), so the two --filter legs are what cover the daemon and the control room. Attribute any red by the merge-base/HEAD delta intersected with this row's owned paths and quote foreign red verbatim (global rail 3). Named verification command for completion: `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`.

VERIFY THE ROSTER ACTUALLY BITES — the integration check only the parent can do, because child 3 wrote the test and a test's author is the worst judge of whether it would have caught the thing it was written for. (a) Confirm the served set is DERIVED from the `*_PATH` constants http-listener-read-dispatch.ts dispatches on, not from a hand-kept list — open the test and read it; a list would be a third copy free to drift (global rail 9). (b) Delete one consumer and confirm the roster reds; add a served route with no consumer and confirm it reds. Both directions, verified by doing them, not by reading the assertion. (c) Confirm the deliberate exclusions (planning.write, graph.supersede, cutover.*, work.*) each carry a stated REASON — an exclusion list without reasons is where a real gap hides. (d) Check whether `REPOSITORY_REMOTE_READ_PATH` is now consumed: it was SERVED but had no browser decoder at plan time (comment-81312c74 on task-19d2329c), and task-e6000b57fd374f78ba074b9f0f0f2c67 was planned to add it. If the roster is red on that route, that is a CORRECT result naming a real gap — record it and coordinate with that row; a green roster achieved by special-casing the route is a failure.

COMPLETE THE ROLL-UP. Name, item by item, which child discharged which DoD clause and where the evidence lives (each child's task.verification, completionSummary and reviewSummary, plus the landing shas). A summary that only says 'children landed' does not discharge the parent. Two things to state EXPLICITLY rather than leave implied: (a) whether the DESIGN PASS comment names what actually CHANGED — the owner's ask was 'we need it for humans not bots', and a comment listing which skills were run without naming the fixes applied does not discharge DoD 4; quote the comment id. (b) Whether the live drive happened, quoting its transcript comment, or saying plainly that it did not. Detail over the 2000-char completionSummary cap goes in a row comment under ~4500 chars, one idea per comment (global rail 14). This row writes no production code: a gap found here is a comment on the owning child plus report_blocked, never a patch.

reopenReason: Spun-out rows are filed in PLANNING (BACKLOG is human-gated and invisible to claim_next_task); created without the status field by mistake.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: REJECTED, planning this as one row: it carries five distinct deliverables (a live Resources screen, two unconsumed daemon reads given screens, a bidirectional route roster, a forensic view, and a design pass with a live drive), which is far past the 12-step/10-file thresholds — task rail 1 mandates a SPIDR split into children under this row. REJECTED, folding the roster test into child 1 or 2: it can only pass once BOTH their screens consume their reads, so it belongs to a third row that depends on them; putting it in either would make that child's own gate depend on its sibling. REJECTED, letting each child run its own live drive and design pass: global rail 21 concentrates the e2e, the design pass and the live drive in one row, which is child 3. REJECTED, planning against the row's own claim that a SOON chip sits at shell-model.ts:111 — measured false; the freeze is the `live` flag at :25 rendered by nav-rail.tsx:112-124, and child 1's description carries the correction so a worker does not hunt a string that is not there.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: MEASURED AT HEAD (branch moe/work-2026-09-04) by architect-20a6d1eb. ONE OF THIS ROW'S OWN PREMISES IS STALE: `grep -n SOON apps/control-room/src/v2/shell/shell-model.ts` = ZERO hits; the string lives in nav-rail.tsx:120 (the StatusChip) and in context-bar.tsx comments. A nav entry is frozen by its `live: boolean` (shell-model.ts:25), and nav-rail.tsx:112-124 renders the chip with testid `cr.nav.<id>.unavailable` — so the rendered marker, not a source grep, is what a test should assert. THE TWO UNCONSUMED READS ARE REAL AND SERVED: http-listener-read-dispatch.ts imports PRODUCT_CONTRACT_GATE_1_READ_PATH with its handler (:11-12) and DOCUMENT_DOSSIER_PATH with its handler (:3); `grep -rn 'gate-1/read' apps/control-room/src` finds nothing outside the proxy list, and `/documents/dossier/read` is already pinned at dev-proxy-paths.ts:16 while the gate-1 route is not. HOW TO ENUMERATE THE SERVED SET: that listener (539 lines) holds NO literal route strings — it imports `*_READ_PATH` constants and dispatches on them, so the roster test derives the served set from those imports rather than a hand-kept list. A GAP THE ROSTER WILL NAME: REPOSITORY_REMOTE_READ_PATH is served (:34) but has no browser decoder and no proxy pin — I recorded that on task-19d2329c as comment-81312c74 and planned task-e6000b57 to add it, so the two rows interact.
planningNotes.risks: BIGGEST RISK — a roster test that cannot fail. If child 3 enumerates the served set from a hand-kept constant rather than from the listener's dispatch, the test passes forever while routes drift out of reach; step 4 requires opening the test and breaking it in both directions rather than reading its assertion. SECOND — the exclusion list. planning.write, graph.supersede, cutover.* and work.* are unconsumed BY DESIGN, and an exclusion list without a reason per entry becomes the place a genuine gap hides; step 4(c) checks for the reasons. THIRD — a green roster bought by special-casing REPOSITORY_REMOTE_READ_PATH, which is exactly the gap the test exists to name; a red roster there is a correct result. FOURTH — the design pass is the clause most easily discharged with a comment that lists skills and no changes; step 5 requires naming what changed and quoting the comment. FIFTH — this row's own SOON premise is false, and a worker who trusts it will grep a file that never held the string and conclude the freeze was already lifted; the correction is in child 1's description and repeated in step 2. SIXTH — credential values on a Resources screen would leak into any operator screenshot; child 1 carries the hostile test for it, and the parent should confirm that arm exists rather than assuming.
